newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares end thin bourse session higher.
newsitem.headline: German shares end thin bourse session higher.

text.p: German shares ended a dull session of bourse trade on Friday slightly higher, as many market players extended the Ascension Thursday holiday into a long weekend, lowering volumes appreciably.

Firm Bunds, strong futures and an upbeat overnight close on Wall Street underpinned sentiment over the session and the DAX index, which measures bourse trade in 30 blue-chip stocks, ended up 10.43 points, or 0.29 percent, at 3,562.41 points.
"We are holding on well here in Germany, even though the dollar is weaker. It is stable, at least," said a Frankfurt trader.
"There are positive factors coming from many sides on the German share market at the moment," Bayerische Vereinsbank said in a research document.
Despite a licking in recent days from the yen and other currencies, the dollar was still seen as having a positive impact on the German share market in the mid-term.
The currency was stable on Friday at around 1.70 marks and Vereinsbank said a rise to 1.75 marks was still possible, while the strength of sterling was also helpful.
"These currency trends, combined with the appealing levels of economic growth abroad, should help improve the outlook for the export sector," said Vereinsbank.
"The clear abatement of volumes in recent days is a cause for concern," analysts at Commerzbank said.
There were some possible clouds on the horizon. "Given an eight-percent rise in the market since the start of April, a bout of profit taking cannot be ruled out," Commerzbank said.

Among the few features of the session was Lufthansa AG, which ended up 1.25 marks, 4.65 percent, at 27.10 marks, still riding a wave of positive sentiment following its upbeat first-quarter 1997 figures on Wednesday.

Shares in electronics giant Siemens AG hit 100 marks for the first time ever, and the share ended at a closing high of 100.10 marks, a rise of 2.65 marks or 2.69 percent, boosted by news of new orders from New Zealand.
